title: Murder on the Orient Express
subtitle: Agatha Christie, 1934 · Hercule Poirot #10
blurb: Celebrated Belgian detective Hercule Poirot is stranded aboard the Orient Express when a fellow passenger, the odious Samuel Ratchett, is found stabbed to death in his locked compartment. With thirteen suspects and a snowdrift holding the train in place, Poirot must untangle a web of false identities and coordinated deception to reveal a truth more extraordinary than any single culprit.

factions.label: The Investigators
factions.description: Hercule Poirot and the railway officials who assist in conducting the inquiry.

factions.label: The Armstrong Circle
factions.description: The twelve passengers — each connected to the Armstrong family tragedy — who collectively planned and executed the murder of Cassetti.

factions.label: Compagnie Internationale des Wagons-Lits
factions.description: Staff and officials of the Orient Express railway company.

characters.name: Hercule Poirot
characters.description: Fastidious Belgian detective famous for his 'little grey cells.' Summoned back to England, he boards the Orient Express and is drawn into the investigation when Ratchett is killed.

characters.name: Samuel Ratchett (Cassetti)
characters.description: A coarse, wealthy American who attempts to hire Poirot as a bodyguard. Revealed after his murder to be Cassetti, the kidnapper and murderer of little Daisy Armstrong.

characters.name: Monsieur Bouc
characters.description: An old friend of Poirot's and a director of the railway company. He facilitates the investigation and ultimately endorses Poirot's alternative explanation to the authorities.

characters.name: Dr. Constantine
characters.description: A Greek doctor travelling on the train who assists Poirot with the medical examination of the body and the forensic aspects of the case.

characters.name: Princess Natalia Dragomiroff
characters.description: An imperious elderly Russian noblewoman and godmother of Sonia Armstrong. One of the conspirators, she provided the crucial handkerchief clue and organised her maid Hildegarde Schmidt's participation.

characters.name: Colonel Arbuthnot
characters.description: A stiff, upright British colonel and close friend of Colonel Armstrong. Part of the conspiracy, he is romantically attached to Mary Debenham.

characters.name: Mary Debenham
characters.description: A cool, composed English governess who was the nursery governess in the Armstrong household at the time of the kidnapping. Her composure under questioning makes her an early suspect.

characters.name: Countess Helena Andrenyi
characters.description: A beautiful Hungarian noblewoman travelling with her husband. Revealed to be Helena Goldenberg, Sonia Armstrong's younger sister, whose identity was concealed to protect her from suspicion.

characters.name: Count Rudolph Andrenyi
characters.description: Helena's devoted husband who altered her passport to conceal her identity and shield her from involvement — though he was not himself part of the conspiracy.

characters.name: Hector MacQueen
characters.description: Ratchett's young American secretary, whose father was the District Attorney ruined by the Cassetti case. One of the conspirators.

characters.name: Edward Masterman
characters.description: Ratchett's English manservant, who was Colonel Armstrong's batman (orderly) during the war. A calm, disciplined participant in the conspiracy.

characters.name: Mrs. Caroline Hubbard (Linda Arden)
characters.description: An apparently talkative and fussy American widow who is in fact the celebrated actress Linda Arden — Sonia Armstrong's mother and the ringleader of the entire conspiracy.

characters.name: Hildegarde Schmidt
characters.description: The Princess's German lady's maid, who was formerly cook in the Armstrong household. She impersonated a Wagons-Lits conductor as part of the conspiracy.

characters.name: Antonio Foscarelli
characters.description: A large, jovial Italian-American who was the Armstrong family's chauffeur. One of the twelve conspirators.

characters.name: Cyrus Hardman
characters.description: Poses as a flamboyant American traveller but is actually a private detective hired to protect Ratchett. Was in love with the Armstrong nursemaid Susanne who died after the kidnapping ordeal.

characters.name: Greta Ohlsson
characters.description: A pious Swedish missionary who was Daisy Armstrong's nurse. Her quiet religious demeanour conceals her role as one of the twelve stabbers.

characters.name: Pierre Michel
characters.description: The French conductor of the Istanbul–Calais coach. His daughter was the Armstrong nursemaid Susanne who died after her wrongful arrest, making him a conspirator despite his official role.

characters.name: Colonel John Armstrong
characters.description: Sonia Armstrong's husband and Daisy's father. Took his own life after his wife and unborn child died in the aftermath of the kidnapping. His tragedy motivates the entire conspiracy; he does not appear in the narrative.

characters.name: Sonia Armstrong
characters.description: Daughter of Linda Arden and mother of Daisy. Died prematurely after the shock of her daughter's murder; her death, along with her husband's suicide, underpins the conspirators' motive.

coverage_note: Colonel Armstrong and Sonia Armstrong are included as deceased catalysts given their structural centrality, though they never appear in the narrative. Minor on-platform characters and background railway staff are omitted. The 'armstrong_conspirators' faction_id is used for the count who was not a stabber but aided the conspiracy by concealing his wife's identity.
notes: Full-spoiler map. The resolution reveals that all twelve passengers connected to the Armstrong household each stabbed Ratchett once, so that no single person bears sole guilt — a verdict Poirot presents alongside a fictional alternative for the authorities. Character count: 19 of a possible ~22 named figures; minor speaking characters omitted under the 25-character cap.
